title: Set skills and competencies to measure
intro: Research for Essentials 2.0: Semester → Courses → skills and competencies. Compare how instructors select course competencies, define measurement, and connect activities to learner evidence. Scenarios (05), events (06), reports (08) and the Canvas hand-off are neighbouring modules.

questions.title: Framework model (central taxonomy vs. free tags vs. both)
Selection UX (tree / search / suggestions) and scale when there are hundreds of items
Reuse of the same competency set across courses and semesters

references.title: Course skill or topic selection
references.question: Q1
references.take: Coursera is a priority education analogue: course topics are presented as selectable structured concepts, supporting taxonomy backed discovery.

references.title: Search and save skills in a skills modal
references.question: Q1
references.take: A central Skills modal uses a constrained search field, helper guidance, and an explicit Save action; this is a direct taxonomy-style selection analogue, though it does not show course ownership.

references.title: Review selected skills as removable chips
references.question: Q1
references.take: Handshake shows a searchable skills field followed by many removable chips and an explicit Save; this is direct taxonomy-selection evidence for reviewing a larger chosen set, though it is profile-based.

references.title: Choose a learning domain from a guided list
references.question: Q2
references.take: Brilliant presents a focused, mutually selectable domain list with one selected state and a Continue step; it is a learner-side taxonomy analogue rather than an admin competency picker.

references.title: Class activity chooser
references.question: Q2
references.take: An education adjacent chooser demonstrates contextual selection of reusable items from a course-facing workflow.

references.title: Skill selection in a learning path
references.question: Q2
references.take: Codecademy is an adjacent learning analogue where a focused skill choice narrows a large catalog before a learner commits.

references.title: Add skills with suggestions and chips
references.question: Q2
references.take: The flow progressively narrows selection from an empty skills input to suggestions, then visible chips and a saved profile; it demonstrates scalable search-and-confirm interaction, as an adjacent HR analogue.

references.title: Editing a curriculum
references.question: Q2
references.take: Teachable’s curriculum editing flow is an adjacent course-management pattern for progressively organizing reusable course units.

references.title: Skill proficiency matrix analogue
references.question: Q3
references.take: An education product analogue suggests grouping skills with visible progress or proficiency states rather than only raw scores.

references.title: Create a rubric with criteria and scoring levels
references.question: Q3
references.take: Google Classroom exposes Use scoring, point values, criterion and level descriptions, plus Add a criterion and Save; this is direct LMS evidence for numeric plus descriptive rubric definition.

references.title: Edit rubric levels and add criteria
references.question: Q3
references.take: A second Google Classroom rubric state makes level editing concrete: required criterion fields, point value, level title and description, plus controls to add levels or criteria before Save.

references.title: Criteria with numeric score and descriptive anchor
references.question: Q3
references.take: A descriptive sentence beside each selected number shows how numeric levels can retain human-readable performance anchors.

references.title: Review worksheet evidence and approve
references.question: Q4
references.take: A teacher opens a submitted worksheet, sees the learner response and comment, then approves or returns it, making evidence review explicit before completion.

references.title: Complete assessment and receive result
references.question: Q4
references.take: A learner assessment journey connects answering items to a final result, a useful analogue for emitting competency scores from activity evidence.

references.title: Course progress path
references.question: Q4
references.take: A compact course path connects individual practice steps to an overall progression state, adjacent evidence for longitudinal competency traceability.

references.title: Create assessment with automatic grading
references.question: Q4
references.take: The flow moves from assessment creation to questions and automatic grading, showing how an activity can own evidence capture and score computation.

references.title: Skill graph impact
references.question: Q4
references.take: A skill graph impact journey is a strong adjacent pattern for showing how an assessment result changes a learner's competency state.

references.title: Skill tree mastery overview
references.question: Q5
references.take: Brilliant presents learning as a navigable skill path, making mastery legible through progress across connected topics.

references.title: Topic progression detail
references.question: Q5
references.take: A topic-level progress view lets learners inspect where they stand within a broader competency journey.

references.title: Mobile skill path
references.question: Q5
references.take: Brilliant’s mobile skill path expresses mastery as a sequence of topic nodes, with the active concept emphasized over the full curriculum.

references.title: Learning progress dashboard
references.question: Q5
references.take: Codecademy is an adjacent analogue for showing learner progress across a structured skills curriculum.

references.title: Skill tracking flow
references.question: Q5
references.take: Codecademy’s multi-screen skill-tracking flow links progress review to deeper skill detail, a useful learner-facing mastery pattern.

references.title: Course path with progress states
references.question: Q5
references.take: Duolingo uses a sequential path with visible completion states so learners can locate current level and next practice target.

references.title: Skill path checkpoint state
references.question: Q5
references.take: Checkpointed units communicate incremental attainment and a clear next action without requiring a dense analytics dashboard.

references.title: Mobile learning path mastery
references.question: Q5
references.take: The mobile path keeps current progress, locked or completed nodes, and the next lesson visible in one compact learner view.

references.title: Skills progress overview
references.question: Q5
references.take: Uxcel provides an adjacent skills-learning reference where progress can be scanned across multiple competencies.

references.title: Courses switching flow
references.question: Q6
references.take: Duolingo’s course switcher flow shows a learner carrying one progress context while choosing among multiple courses, an adjacent reuse and continuity pattern.

references.title: Save a document as a reusable template
references.question: Q6
references.take: Hello Ivy makes reuse explicit: page options expose Save as template, a preview-and-controls modal captures template details, and a confirmation toast closes the loop; this is a direct reusable-set analogue.

references.title: Course template reuse control
references.question: Q6
references.take: Teachable is an adjacent course-management analogue for carrying a structured course setup forward as a reusable template.

references.title: Reusable learning track setup
references.question: Q6
references.take: Uxcel offers an adjacent skills platform pattern for packaging learning structure so it can be applied consistently across cohorts.
